other_items.magnitude: net +0.34 to +0.61 W/m2 global mean; -2.0 W/m2 over ocean to +8.7 over salt crust
other_items.note: PRICED 2026-08-17, DUST-2, at the burden DUST-1 produces: land-mean optical depth 0.376. See analysis/dust_forcing.json and exoplasim/scripts/dust_forcing.py. Shortwave -8.7 W/m2 over ocean, -5.6 over vegetated land, -0.1 over playa and +2.0 over salt crust; longwave +6.7 W/m2 everywhere as a clear-sky-window UPPER bound. Global mean net +0.34 to +0.61 across the size bracket, which is below the 1.5 W/m2 reopening threshold only because ocean cooling cancels land warming -- the net spans 11 W/m2 by surface and that is what drives circulation. THE EARLIER SIGN CLAIM IS SUPERSEDED. This entry said the sign was resolved and cooling; that was a shortwave-only result. With the thermal infrared included the sign is surface-dependent and POSITIVE over the bright closed-basin fill that makes this world unusual. TWO CORRECTIONS TO THIS ENTRY'S OWN EARLIER CLAIMS. Aerosols are NOT unswitchable: aero_ini is called at plasim.f90:190 and reads aero_nl with l_aerorad and aerofile use-associated from radmod, so reading the namelist does set them, and Model.configure writes l_aerorad, aerofile, L_AERO, l_source, apart, rhop and fcoeff. What is true is that the aerosol acts in the two SHORTWAVE bands only and the longwave solver has no aerosol term at all, so switching it on as shipped would apply -3.4 to -4.0 W/m2 of global-mean cooling against a true +0.34 to +0.61: an error of 4.0 to 4.3 W/m2, against 21 W/m2 for the entire 0.85-to-0.95 stellar sweep that produced a 33 K range. That is DUST-3's problem and it is why DUST-2 came first.
